observations.note: Luis Hernandez replaced Mickey Gall on two days notice
Gall withdrew with a medical issue; Luis Hernandez stepped in on two days notice

Coach Carlos Costa says the camp was built around Shevchenko for months - a full technical study, focused on takedown defence, timing entries and distance control - and the focus was changed completely when the UFC said she was out.
Promoted into a vacant-title main event after Shevchenko withdrew with a back and shoulder ligament injury. Reporting does not describe it as a short-notice booking.

First bout since December 2025, when he beat Cejudo. Says the inactivity was not injury: 'I've been waiting for the better part of a year. I've been spoken to about a bunch of fights, but I guess people have had better plans.'

UFC debut, and his first MMA bout since 20 February 2025 - about nineteen months. Describes himself as having been 'semi-retired' during the inactive spell in ONE. Had a professional boxing bout in September 2025.
Disclosed in an interview during this camp that the mother of his child has been diagnosed with leukemia.

Combat Press: Reynoso, a TUF alternate, was originally set to face fellow alternate Wushamo Hailai (DWCS Week 6, Sept 15); Tapology lists that bout cancelled after Hailai withdrew, reason not given. Rebooked against Bertolso two weeks later.
Sherdog lists her last fight as the LFA strawweight title win over Lany Silva at LFA 216 on 2025-09-05, so she has been out about 12.8 months.
Back down to featherweight: his last fight (CW 209, 2026-07-04) was at a 161 lb catchweight, where he weighed 160.7; about 12 weeks later he made 145.5 for tonight.

Cageside Press (2026-06-07): after beating Edmen Shahbazyan at UFC Vegas 118, Allen said he wants a title rematch with champion Sean Strickland and is open to Nassourdine Imavov or the Du Plessis-Usman winner. Said in June, before this bout was booked.
Cageside Press (2026-09-01): this is Duncan's first UFC main event, scheduled for five rounds; he comes in on a five-fight win streak that includes Jared Cannonier and Roman Dolidze.

MMA Sucka, relaying an MMA Junkie Radio interview: Camilo said he studied Herbert's loss to Ilia Topuria and that "Herbert sometimes struggles on the ground, and I see few spaces I can catch him striking, also."
Heavy.com, previewing this bout: Wellmaker "recently switched camps to American Top Team" after two straight UFC losses (GIDStats reported the move on 2026-05-29).

BoxingNews: Meerschaert, 38, moves up to light heavyweight for this fight after five straight losses at middleweight; he missed weight by 4 lb for his last fight (vs Jacob Malkoun, May 2026, held at a 190 lb catchweight per Cageside Press).
RotoWire, citing Marcel Dorff of Heavy: Artur Minev withdrew for an undisclosed reason and Prado now faces Ismael Bonfim, who steps in on short notice. No notice period is stated.
Heavy: Prado drops back to lightweight for this fight after three welterweight decision losses (Jake Matthews, Nikolay Veretennikov, Charles Radtke); no win since 2023.
RotoWire, citing Marcel Dorff of Heavy: Bonfim "steps in on short notice" to replace Artur Minev against Francisco Prado. The notice period is not stated.

Official weigh-ins 2026-10-09: Bonfim 163.5 lb, 7.5 lb over the 156 lb non-title lightweight limit; fined 25% of his purse; Bloody Elbow reports the bout goes ahead at a catchweight. Prado made weight (155). His third UFC weight miss.
Official weigh-ins 2026-10-09 (Cageside Press): Ribeiro 208.5 lb, 2.5 lb over the 206 lb non-title light heavyweight limit; fined 20% of his purse to Felipe Franco (205); the bout goes ahead.
Official weigh-ins 2026-10-09 (Cageside Press): Souza 117 lb, 1 lb over the 116 lb non-title strawweight limit; fined 20% of her purse to Loopy Godinez (115.5); the bout goes ahead.
Home of Fight interview (via EssentiallySports and MMASucka): Price says the UFC offered him one more fight he could not turn down and that this will be his last; he had retired in March 2026.
Heavy: Price returns from a brief retirement, announced in March 2026 after a first-round submission loss to Michael Chiesa at UFC Seattle, about six months before this bout; four straight losses.
RotoWire: Frye pulled out of his July 18, 2026 bout with Alvin Hines for undisclosed reasons; RJ Harris - his opponent here - replaced him on about a week's notice and won by first-round TKO.
AgentMMA's earlier preview listed Franco vs Alexander Poppeck for this card; current listings show Brendson Ribeiro. No named outlet reports why or when Poppeck left.

MMA Junkie (Nolan King), via Cageside Press: Blanchfield withdrew from this bout's original UFC 330 date (Aug 15) with an undisclosed injury - her first UFC withdrawal - and it moved to Edmonton. No report on her health since.
MMASucka (outlet framing, not her quote): Blanchfield wants a flyweight title shot against Valentina Shevchenko, and a win here would move her closer.
MMASucka: her bout with Blanchfield moved from UFC 330 (Aug 15) to Edmonton after Blanchfield's injury withdrawal - same opponent, about two months later, now in front of a Canadian crowd.
theScore and Low Kick MMA: Malott headlines in Canada for the third straight time (six of his eight UFC fights in Canada), on a four-fight win streak capped by a TKO of Gilbert Burns in April.
MMASucka: Buckley comes in on two straight decision losses (Kamaru Usman, Sean Brady) after six straight wins; outlets say his top-10 ranking is at stake.
Cageside Press (2026-08-10): Barriault is 1-5 in his last six fights.
Cageside Press (2026-08-11): UFC debut; he earned the contract on Dana White's Contender Series (Sept 2025, submission of Magno Dias) and has not fought since; four-fight win streak.

AgentMMA's booking story calls Nallo vs Landwehr a featherweight bout while event listings have it at lightweight - the weight class is not settled. Landwehr comes in on three straight losses (Dooho Choi, Morgan Charriere, Cub Swanson).
RotoWire: Diniz withdrew from a June 2026 bout with Jose Luiz 'Montanha' (UFC Vegas 119) with an undisclosed injury; nothing reported on his recovery.
RotoWire: his last fight was a second-round TKO loss to Mario Pinto on 2025-10-11 - about a year out of competition.
AgentMMA: Galanti (8-1) replaces Gilbert Urbina, who was ruled out, against Julien Leblanc in his UFC debut. The notice period is not stated.
AgentMMA: original opponent Gilbert Urbina was ruled out (no reason given); Leblanc now faces UFC newcomer Nick Galanti.
RotoWire, citing Marcel Dorff of Heavy: Louie Sutherland is out (listed injury, undisclosed); Mahjoub now faces UFC newcomer Joel Faglier.
RotoWire, citing Marcel Dorff of Heavy: Faglier replaces Louie Sutherland against Javad Mahjoub in his UFC debut. The notice period is not stated.
EssentiallySports: original opponent Jamey-Lyn Horth withdrew after a training injury and was not medically cleared after an MRI; Cerminara now faces Mackenzie Stiller.
Low Kick MMA: her first fight since a decision loss to Maycee Barber at UFC 299 (March 2024) - about two years and seven months out.
Low Kick MMA: she gave birth to her first child in August 2025; this is her first fight as a mother.
AgentMMA and EssentiallySports: Stiller replaces Jamey-Lyn Horth, who withdrew with a training injury, against Katlyn Cerminara in her UFC debut. No named outlet states the notice period.
Cageside Press interview (2026-10-01): nearly two years out since a decision loss to Cody Gibson (Nov 2024); he said the time went to rehab on a knee injury and that he kept training and sparring.
Cageside Press interview (2026-10-01): he calls this fight "kind of like a redemption story" after an unhappy last performance, also in Edmonton.
Heavy: his UFC debut comes more than a year after his Contender Series KO of Raphael Uchegbu (Sept 2025); no reason given for the gap.

Weigh-ins settle the weight class: Landwehr 155, Nallo 155.5 - a lightweight bout (156 non-title limit), Landwehr's first at 155. Sherdog and Hot Takes report the weights; all 26 fighters made weight.
Cageside Press, media day: three straight losses finally pushed him up from 145 to 155 - "Now, down three, man I've got nothing to lose." UFC.com ran the same story.
MiddleEasy: Robbie Lawler will corner him in Edmonton after about ten weeks of training at Kill Cliff FC.

Cageside Press: says he never gets over losses and must rein in his eagerness to finish after the first-round stoppage by Jai Herbert in his April UFC debut; MiddleEasy says he plans a more patient approach.
MMA Mania's live weigh-in report (via Yahoo): 186.5 on his first attempt, then made 186 - exactly the non-title limit - after stripping down behind a curtain. He made weight; no fine.
MiddleEasy: expects to dominate Barriault and says he will not get into a brawl, because long exchanges build Barriault's momentum.
Cageside Press: says he feels more pressure for this fight than for the White House card, where Bo Nickal stopped him in round 1.
Yahoo Sports weigh-in recap: one of the two scale scares - stripped down and weighed in behind a box, then made 136, exactly the non-title limit.
Cageside Press: at 36 he calls this the last chapter of his career and wants "good fights, good guys"; he comes in on a two-fight skid. MiddleEasy reported the same.
MiddleEasy: details his move to the Fight Sports gym, and says this is one of two fights left on his UFC contract.
MMA Mania: answering Buckley's popularity jibe, Malott said Buckley "would never headline in Canada without me"; at media day he told Cageside Press "this is my show" and called it a very good camp.
Cageside Press, media day: says Malott took the fight to raise his own profile - "You're trying to become the A-side"; this is Buckley's third UFC headliner.
Cageside Press, media day: calls it a title eliminator - "whoever wins this fight does expect a title shot"; Sherdog says she wants a title rematch with champion Natalia Silva in Toronto.
BJPenn.com: expects Blanchfield to turn to wrestling "once she feels these hands".
MiddleEasy, media day: the UFC has not promised her a title shot with a win; BJPenn.com says she expects a finish to earn one.
Cageside Press: UFC debut after the Contender Series; says he got the Nelson fight on about five or six weeks' notice and predicts a performance-of-the-night bonus.
Cageside Press: wants to "spoil the party" at Jourdain's debut and says he will out-class him if his game plan holds.
Yahoo News Canada: the Edmonton heavyweight finally gets a UFC fight in his hometown, at Rogers Place.
Cageside Press (2026-09-18): Arnold Allen is out of their UFC 333 bout; former Oktagon champion Losene Keita replaces him.
MMA Junkie via MMASucka: chose to stay on the card against the unranked Keita rather than wait for a ranked opponent - "sitting around and waiting for a ranked guy is not in my agenda."
Cageside Press (2026-09-18): replaces Arnold Allen against Aaron Pico about five weeks out, soon after his KO win at UFC Paris (2026-09-05).
Heavy: missed weight for his originally scheduled UFC debut (against Patricio Pitbull) before getting a second chance.
AgentMMA: before the booking, offered to fight any top-15 featherweight on short notice.
RotoWire (citing Heavy On Sports) lists him with an arm injury - a Paulo Costa high kick damaged his left arm in the TKO loss at UFC 327 (2026-04-11).
AgentMMA: Robert Whittaker said he broke Krylov's jaw in the round-3 TKO at UFC 329 (2026-07-11); another report said doctors found no fracture.
Newsweek (from 10 News): whether he retires depends on how UFC 333 goes - he would walk away after a bad beating; no plans to retire now.
The National (2026-10-06): "a nice long camp"; says his grappling prep with Craig Jones gives him confidence against an elite wrestler like Evloev.
PredictionHunt (2026-09-04): said on Sept 2 he cuts about 12 kg to make 145 lb and plans to move to lightweight after this fight.
MMA Junkie via MMASucka: says he will not chase a finish and wants to win over 25 minutes on the scorecards.
Low Kick MMA: nine-hour surgery on damaged lumbar discs after the UFC 323 title win (Dec 2025); in mid-June a teammate said he was about two months from training.
AgentMMA: back to pad work after back-surgery recovery; first fight since UFC 323 (2025-12-06).
AgentMMA: trilogy camp opened in Kislovodsk under Kairat Nurmaganbetov (partners incl. Kurban Gadzhiev, Asaf Chopurov), then moved to Dubai.
Yardbarker: added a new coach ('Jesse') for private sessions at Q MMA, Las Vegas, preparing for the Yan trilogy.
Heavy: lost to Henry Cejudo by technical fall in the RAF 12 freestyle wrestling main event (Aug 2026), during this fight's build-up.
Cageside Press (Sep 14): replaced Brian Ortega against Renato Moicano in the main event.
Cageside Press (Sep 14): Ortega out; Moicano now meets Tom Nolan.
Heavy: accepted the co-main against Randy Brown on 12 days' notice, replacing Carlos Leal; fought on Oct 3.
MMA Sucka: Leal out; Jacobe Smith steps in.
Heavy: replaced Gaston Bolanos (cut in training) against Francis Marshall.
Heavy: Bolanos withdrew with a cut from training; Dakota Hope steps in.
Heavy: medically cleared; returns from a layoff since Nov 2024 for his middleweight debut.
Yardbarker: withdrew from the original Durden booking at UFC 329 (July) with an undisclosed injury; rebooked for Oct 31.
UFC.com reports Cortes Acosta accepted the new UFC Vegas 124 headliner against Walker on about a week and a half's notice, after Sean Brady's withdrawal scrapped Bonfim vs. Brady.
BJPenn.com reports Cortes Acosta predicted a violent finish of Walker at UFC Vegas 124 media day, saying 'he doesn't have a chin. It's like a doorbell; it's easy to hit it.'
MiddleEasy reports Cortes Acosta said in a Nov. 5 fight-week interview that he wants a first-round finish of Walker ('I need to knock out this guy in the first round').
Cageside Press reports Cortes Acosta said during UFC Vegas 124 fight week that he wants to get back what the judges have taken from him after two straight decision losses.
Sherdog reports Walker had planned to take it slow at heavyweight but took the short-notice UFC Vegas 124 main event against Cortes Acosta when the UFC called after Sean Brady's withdrawal.
MiddleEasy reports Walker said the short-notice UFC Vegas 124 main event against Cortes Acosta was too good to refuse.
UFC.com reports Jandiroba said her UFC 321 title loss to Dern made her a better fighter and that the Suarez fight will be won by the better mixed martial artist, not by grappling comparisons.

Yahoo Sports (MMA Junkie) reports Smith said at UFC Fight Night 293 media day that this is the last fight on his contract ('After this fight, I'm a free agent'), that the UFC had not approached him about a new deal, and that he was surprised it was not renewed.
AgentMMA reports Smith confirmed that UFC Vegas 124 is the final fight on his current UFC contract and that the UFC had not yet talked to him about re-signing.

Yahoo Sports (MMA Junkie), headlined 'Elijah Smith guarantees bonus, new contract at UFC Fight Night 293', reports Smith said '(The contract is) coming, 100 percent' and promised a performance bonus to strengthen his case for a new deal.
MiddleEasy reports Smith said, in a UFC interview dated Nov 6, that his surgically repaired hand is fully healed before his return against Davey Grant.
UFC.com's fight-week feature says a hand injury that needed surgery forced Smith to the sidelines after his win over SuYoung You, and that he says the hand is now fully healed.
UFC.com says Smith returns after time away since his March 2026 win, with hand surgery limiting his training in the interim.
MiddleEasy, writing up the UFC's Nov 6 interview, says Smith's layoff was shaped by injury, fatherhood and music.
UFC.com's feature, headlined 'Elijah Smith Out to Remind Himself Who He Is', frames Smith's return as being about reconnecting with his own confidence and remembering he is the same fighter.
Yahoo Sports (MMA Junkie) reports Grant said he loves fighting and is 'going to be absolutely devastated' when he retires.

BBC Sport (via Yahoo Sports), in 'What a ride - Meet the UFC's longest-serving Brit', reports Grant, 40, has given no indication the Smith fight will be his last but says he is looking forward to retirement when it comes.
NoCutNews (Nov 5 interview), headlined 'Better Than Him? In Everything! Worse? In Nothing!', reports Ko expects to beat Turman by knockout.
A UFC.com fight-week video for UFC Fight Night: Cortes Acosta vs Walker is titled 'Seokhyeon Ko: I'm Definitely Going To Knock Him Out'.

NoCutNews reports Ko dismissed questions about pressure over a possible UFC release, pointing out he has had only three UFC fights. NoCutNews ('Better Than Him? In Everything!...' interview) reports that ahead of the Turman bout Ko has focused on striking training to become a more complete fighter, and that he warned of Turman's kicks and surprise submissions.

The Herald Business reports that Ko married the month before, skipped his honeymoon, and put his frustration over his first UFC loss into fixing weaknesses and harder striking drills for the Turman fight.
Rotowire reports that Turman has not fought since a December 2023 submission loss to Jared Gooden and faces Seok Hyeon Ko at UFC Vegas 124 on Nov. 7.

MMA Fighting (via Yahoo Sports) reports Turman said he had four shoulder surgeries during his layoff and two had to be redone (an infection on the right, a failed left-shoulder operation); the interview was given before the cancelled July 2026 return, and the same layoff continues into this fight.

UFCalendar reports (Oct. 27) that the Kondratavicius vs. Petroski bout moved from the Oct. 31 Moicano vs. Nolan card to this Nov. 7 card, so Petroski, whose original opponent Azamat Bekoev withdrew, has a new opponent and a new date.
MMA Sucka reports that Azamat Bekoev said in a statement that an anaphylactic reaction, which made him pass out in a store, forced him out of his UFC Vegas 123 fight with Andre Petroski.
Agent MMA reports that Wes Schultz was removed from his UFC Vegas 124 bout with Kondratavicius and that Bekoev withdrew from Petroski's fight, so the two were paired for Nov. 7.
Sherdog reports Elekana said at UFC media day, 'I'm looking for a twister in this fight' against Lucas Fernando at UFC Vegas 124.
Sherdog reports Elekana said he is 'trying to be the Charles Oliveira of the light heavyweight division' and is chasing submission finishes going into the Fernando fight.

Tribuna do Sertao (Oct 15, 2026) interview previewing Delano's Nov 7 Las Vegas bout against Kyrgyz featherweight Murtazali Magomedov, his second UFC fight. Delano calls Magomedov resilient ('ele nao se entrega', 'he doesn't give up') but says the opponent has never faced a fighter willing to stick to a patient game plan. This is pre-fight confidence and game-plan talk, with no camp, injury or weight news.

Sports Gambling Podcast's UFC Vegas 124 prelim preview (it picks Jonny Parsons +186 over Souza) says Souza's last bout was a short-notice fight in late May (May 30, 2026) and that he is being turned around for this fight only a few months later. The outlet frames this as a quick turnaround; the actual gap is about 5 months. The short-notice part refers to his earlier fight, not this one.

Agent MMA reports Lucas Brennan withdrew from his UFC Vegas 124 bout with Bashi after tearing his ACL in the final two weeks of camp, which left Bashi without an opponent for a time. RotoWire, citing Marcel Dorff of Heavy, reports Bashi 'will now fight Carlos Calderon at UFC Vegas 124 on Saturday.'

RotoWire, citing Marcel Dorff of Heavy, reports Calderon will now fight Austin Bashi at UFC Vegas 124 on Saturday. He replaces Lucas Brennan, who withdrew after tearing his ACL in the final two weeks of camp (Agent MMA). Only this one outlet chain carries the Calderon booking. No outlet gives the booking date or calls it short notice, so the notice period is unknown.

UFC.com official weigh-in results: McKinney missed the 156-lb lightweight non-title limit for his bout with Jim Miller (weighed 160.2, 4.2 lb over); he forfeits 30% of his purse to Miller and the fight proceeds at catchweight.
Sherdog's UFC 334 weigh-in report says McKinney missed weight by 4.2 lb and will be fined a percentage of his purse; the bout with Jim Miller goes ahead.

Heavy reports McKinney issued a statement after his 160.2-lb miss announcing UFC 334 will be his last fight at lightweight, citing difficulty making 155, and that he will move up to welterweight afterwards.

UFC.com official weigh-in results: Diaz came in above the 136-lb bantamweight non-title limit for his bout with Alatengheili; he forfeits 20% of his purse to Alatengheili and the fight proceeds at catchweight.
Sherdog's UFC 334 weigh-in report says Diaz missed weight by 0.4 lb (136.4; Alatengheili 135.6) and will be fined a percentage of his purse.
UFC.com's UFC 334 card-updates page says Adrian Yanez was removed from his bantamweight bout with Diaz due to injury and Alatengheili replaces him.
Bloody Elbow (Nov. 6) reports Alatengheili agreed to fight Juan Diaz at UFC 334 on eight days' notice, replacing Adrian Yanez.
Sherdog reports Baisangur Susurkaev withdrew from his UFC 334 middleweight bout with Johnson and Cesar Almeida replaced him; no reason for the withdrawal was given in the reports found.

Sherdog's weigh-in report lists Johnson vs. Almeida as a 190-lb catchweight, no longer middleweight; Johnson weighed 189 and Almeida 189.6, both inside the limit. No outlet in this pass says which side asked for the catchweight.
UFC.com's official weigh-in results list Almeida at 189.6 and Johnson at 189 for a bout now contracted at a 190-lb catchweight instead of middleweight.
Boxing News reports Almeida replaced Baisangur Susurkaev as Donte Johnson's UFC 334 opponent. Almeida is a replacement; no outlet in this pass states his notice period.
Bloody Elbow (Sept. 15) reports Tom Aspinall's eye injury cancelled the planned Gane rematch at UFC 334 and gives a new Aspinall recovery timeline; Josh Hokit is now Gane's opponent.
Sherdog reports Harrison said she questioned whether she would recover from the neck surgery that postponed her January UFC 324 bout with Nunes ('But I'm back').
Yahoo Sports reports Harrison said she was on the verge of permanent nerve damage before surgery on herniated discs in her neck.
Bloody Elbow (Nov. 13) reports videos of Harrison's depleted appearance on the scale at the UFC 334 weigh-in (she made 135.0) went viral and drew fan concern ('looks like a corpse').
CBS Sports reports Harrison said the chance to face Nunes was the only reason she endured the neck-surgery recovery, and that retiring after Saturday, win or lose, remains a possibility.
Boxing News reports Nunes weighs in for UFC 334 after a three-year absence; she retired after beating Irene Aldana at UFC 289 in June 2023.
Yahoo Sports, headlined 'Amanda Nunes UFC 334 return isn't a one-off', reports Nunes said she plans to defend the belt if she wins rather than fight once.

Cageside Press (Nov. 12), headlined 'Amanda Nunes Reveals What Really Brought Her Out of Retirement for UFC 334', reports she said she had been burned out when she retired and came to miss being a fighter.

Sherdog reports Borralho said he broke a rib two weeks before his UFC 326 win over Reinier de Ridder and hid its severity from the UFC; it had not healed 10 weeks later, he needed emergency surgery, and the recovery forced him out of a UFC 330 bout with Joe Pyfer.
Bloody Elbow (Nov. 7) reports Borralho revealed he hid an injury that later required emergency surgery from the UFC before his last win (the broken rib before De Ridder).
Yahoo Sports reports Borralho called for a top-10 opponent at UFC 334 and believes he is 'one or two' wins away from a title shot.
Yahoo Sports reports Belgaroui said at UFC 334 media day, 'I think I'm the best striker in the middleweight division for sure' and 'I truly believe 100 percent I will knock him out.'

Yahoo Sports, headlined 'Kevin Holland sees the end of the road coming into UFC 334: We're almost done, 100%', reports Holland said he just signed a new UFC deal that he will fight out, and then that's it.
Cageside Press (Nov. 12) reports Hasan said of Luis Gurule ahead of UFC 334, 'I don't see anything special.'

Yahoo Sports, headlined 'Luis Gurule intent on derailing Bilal Hasan hype train at UFC 334', reports Gurule said at media day he does not want to look back on a career without having fought anybody good.
Cageside Press (Nov. 12) reports Thompson has no regrets about announcing UFC 334 against Radtke as his retirement fight.

Yahoo Sports, headlined ''Wonderdad' Now: Stephen 'Wonderboy' Thompson Says UFC 334 Is His Last Fight - Baby Girl Changed Everything', reports Thompson said becoming a father to a baby daughter drove his decision to retire.
UFC.com's feature 'The Tao of Jim Miller' says McKinney is Miller's 60th pro fight and frames his remaining goals around reaching 50 UFC appearances and 30 UFC wins.

Fightsports.tv, headlined 'UFC 334 Is A Farewell Night For 2 MMA Veterans', reports Miller intends to retire after his 50th UFC appearance regardless of results and quotes him: 'I am ready to move on.'

Yahoo Sports ('Moving on up') reports Costa makes his lightweight debut against Gordon after saying, following his May loss to Arnold Allen, that he would no longer compete at featherweight because of difficult weight cuts. He made 155.4 at the weigh-in.
UFC.com's athlete profile says Sanches was scheduled to make his UFC debut in March 2026 but withdrew with an arm injury.
Sherdog's prospect watch says Sanches was later scheduled to face Tofiq Musayev but withdrew due to an injury it does not specify.
Bloody Elbow (Oct. 2) reports Sanches finally booked his UFC debut more than a year after earning a contract on Dana White's Contender Series (KO of Chasen Blair, Sept. 2025).
